title: A key MIS 3 Mammuthus–Coelodonta Fauna in Northeast China: Chronological framework and paleoecological implications of the Dabusu Fauna
content:
ABSTRACT

The causes of Late Pleistocene megafaunal extinctions remain debated, with climatic instability and human impacts as leading hypotheses. Well-dated regional records are essential for testing these hypotheses. A complex fossil assemblage predominantly composed of grassland mammals, the Mammuthus–Coelodonta Faunal Complex, is preserved in the Upper Pleistocene of Northeast China. In this study, we focused on the particularly rich fauna of the Dabusu Formation in Qian'an, Jilin Province, and combined morphology, biomolecular identifications using Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) techniques, and Accelerator Mass Spectrometry for carbon-14 (AMS-14C) dating in order to gain a better understanding of the evolutionary trends among terrestrial mammals of this period. Our results show that the fossil materials from the Dabusu Fauna have an extended chronological range, from 51–22 k cal a BP, predating previous estimates by approximately 20 000 years and confirming its activity primarily during Marine Isotope Stage 3 (MIS 3). Paleoecological analyses indicate the preservation of a steppe-dominated assemblage, populated mainly by grazers (59.08%). The proportion of extinct taxa is relatively high (40.9%), but this value is descriptive and not a time-standardized extinction rate; it should not, by itself, be taken as evidence of reduced ecosystem resilience. The new expanded chronology provides a crucial framework for understanding evolutionary trends in the region, but the exact drivers of faunal turnover remain poorly understood and require further investigation with paleoecological proxies. This study highlights the Dabusu faunal assemblage as a key MIS 3 record within the Mammuthus–Coelodonta Fauna of Northeast Asia.
